scope:
Package K1c-2 (KERNEL ONLY): make the graph perspective 'sent_to_model' real, so the receipt of an answer can be shown IN THE GRAPH (the owner's rule: the graph is the hub, everything is data; the sheet 'Co wyslalismy' has a button 'Pokaz w grafie' that is visible but disabled because the kernel answers Unsupported). Branch claude/m1-w0 is at b15180c8 (K1c-1: the estimate and the guard are one number with a named base). The web side is the NEXT package (K1c-3) - do not touch loom/web except if a unit test of the kernel contract needs a fixture.
FACTS (already checked): (1) loom/data/runtime/graph_views.pack declares the perspective 'sent_to_model' (relations ['sent_to_model'], ~line 1751) with "source": "receipt" (~line 1767) and a relation type 'sent_to_model' (~line 1327: 'Source (a message) sent target (an element) to the model.'). (2) loom/src/views/perspectives.cpp ~line 232 renders a perspective by its 'source' mechanism: 'scope_chain', 'history', 'catalogue' exist, 'receipt' does NOT, so the result is Errc::Unsupported "unknown source mechanism 'receipt'". Read the neighbours (the 'catalogue' branch ~line 212 and its projection::render_catalogue in loom/src/graph/projection.cpp) and follow their output shape so that graph.navigate / the existing renderers work unchanged. (3) The receipt (loom.context_receipt/1, stored in messages.metadata.context_trace.receipt of the USER message; ops 'context.receipt'; builder in loom/src/chat/context_format.cpp ~line 580 and chat_engine.cpp ~lines 1206-1530) has sections[{class, items[{ref,label,source_kind,why,tokens_est}], tokens_est}] and dropped[]. Most items are AGGREGATES today: refs 'system_prompt', 'guardian_rules', 'memory_tree', 'graph_memory', 'unified_context', 'knowledge_context', 'question'; only history items carry real message ids (ref = message id, source_kind 'message:<level>'). GraphMemorySelector::select_context (loom/include/loom/graph_memory.h line 48) returns a STRING, so the ids of the graph nodes it chose are lost.
WHAT TO BUILD, in this order, commit after each: (A) THE PROJECTION. Implement the 'receipt' source mechanism: for focus = a message id (the user message of the request, or the answer - resolve the answer to its request_msg_id exactly as ops 'context.receipt' does) render the stored receipt as a graph: the message node, one node per receipt ITEM, links type 'sent_to_model' message -> item (weight = tokens_est, metadata = class/section, why, source_kind). An item whose ref is a real node/message id of the database resolves to THAT node (so the owner can continue navigating from it); an aggregate item becomes a derived node (stable id such as sent:<msg_id>:<ref>, kind from source_kind, label from the receipt, flagged derived=true in its metadata) - nothing is written to the database (a projection, computed on demand from the stored receipt, reversible by deleting the branch); dropped[] are shown as nodes/links of a second relation or as metadata of the section, your choice, but they must be visible (what was NOT sent and why), not silently omitted. A message with no receipt (written before M1, or context_receipt_store=never) answers with the same words as ops 'context.receipt' (missing_reason before_m1) and an empty graph, not an error. (B) PER-ELEMENT ITEMS, if (A) is committed and green: make the graph and memory sections list the ELEMENTS, not only the aggregate: add an additive detailed selection API next to select_context in GraphMemorySelector (e.g. select_context_detailed returning the same text byte-for-byte PLUS the node ids and labels it used; select_context keeps its signature and its output - loom/tests/fixtures/golden/chat_request_legacy.json must stay byte-identical and is NEVER regenerated) and the list of active memory node ids from MemoryEngine; the receipt items become one per element (ref = node id, label, tokens_est of that node's share) bounded by the existing context_receipt_max_bytes (when over the bound keep the aggregate item and set truncated, as the receipt already does). Receipt schema loom.context_receipt/1 may only grow additively; update the receipt docs and the Python<->Loom compat expectations if the stored metadata changes shape (it is on by default now). If (B) does not fit in the budget, stop after (A), say exactly what is left and why.
DECISIONS ARE YOURS (R1-R53: everything configurable, defaults are presets, no invented limits, nothing hidden silently); write them with how to reverse them into docs/reports/INDEX.md under 'S1 / M1-K1c2'. Any word the owner will read (labels of derived nodes, the empty-graph sentence) is DATA in a pack (pl + en), no literals in C++ except ids. If a new web API route literal is needed run the registry chain (python3 loom/tools/gen_graph_interfaces.py -> python3 loom/src/model/gen_runtime_profiles.py (then --check) -> re-pin sha256 of graph/interfaces.pack in loom/data/data_domains.pack -> ctest -R 'graph_entry|kb_pack|kb_data_domains|runtime_profile|onboarding_pack|graph_proj'); graph.navigate with perspectives=['sent_to_model'] should need none - say 'no new route literal' if so. Tests: a kernel test (one file per area: loom/tests/test_graph_sent_to_model.cpp or an extension of the perspectives test) with a synthetic conversation: send a message with a mock model, read the receipt, render the perspective and check nodes/links/weights/derived flags, the dropped part, the no-receipt case, and that nothing was written to nodes/links (row counts equal before and after); if (B) is done: the element ids in the receipt exist as nodes and the text of the request is byte-identical with and without the detailed selection.
accept: cmake --build --preset dev (once per change, in the background, polled with short calls) succeeds; ctest --preset dev -R 'context_receipt|context_modify|chat_request|graph_|perspective|views|runtime_profile|onboarding_pack|kb_pack|kb_data_domains|abi_compat|compat' green (the compat set must stay green: if you changed what the receipt stores, say so); python3 tools/clang_inc_check.py loom/build/dev (copy it from /home/user/chatadhd/tools/ into the scratchpad if absent in this worktree) and python3 tools/lint_asan_range_for.py 51684e78 show nothing new; pushed to origin claude/m1-w0. The card pastes: the rendered projection of one synthetic receipt (node and link counts, one sample link with its weight, the derived-node flag, the dropped part), the 'no receipt' answer, the decisions with how to reverse them, and exactly what is left.
rules_extra: Shared machine: never kill processes by name; record the pid/port you started. Do NOT run the full gate (S1 does). CACHE RULE: no single tool call longer than ~4 minutes - run builds and tests in the background and poll with short calls. One native build at a time (disk is small: no second build tree; use loom/build/dev of this worktree). Keep context small: grep and line ranges, never dump big files. ASAN pitfall: never range-for over .at()/.value()/operator[] of a by-value temporary - bind to a named const first. Generated *.inc data keeps explicit lengths (the generators already do). Tests must not depend on speed or order. Private data: synthetic data only; never read docs/exports or eval/real-holdout-key. Do not touch loom/web (next package) or loom/android/smoke/* (owned by the parallel session). Texts for the owner in plain Polish and English; nothing described as working that is only planned.
